question.text: Section XIV of the PPM template requires disclosure of disciplinary history. Disciplinary history of which set of entities must be disclosed?

answer.text: Only the Sponsor and the Manager
Sponsor, Manager, Trustee, Associates of Sponsor, Associates of Manager, Directors/Partners of Sponsor, Directors/Partners of Manager, and Directors/Partners of Trustee
All investors holding more than 10% of units

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.5 (Section XIV — Disciplinary history), disclosure is required for: Sponsor, Manager, Trustee, Associates of Sponsor, Associates of Manager, Directors/Partners of Sponsor, Directors/Partners of Manager, and Directors/Partners of Trustee. This wide net ensures LPs see the full regulatory/enforcement track record of the ecosystem around the AIF. The Trap: Restricting to Manager only or Manager+Sponsor misses the Trustee and the associates/directors/partners. Investors are NOT disclosed-parties in Section XIV. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test disciplinary disclosure at recall level. XIX-C drills into the full scope of parties covered — matters in drafting and update cycles. Manager's Pro-Tip: Set up an annual self-declaration template for each party listed above — collecting updated disciplinary disclosures one-by-one at PPM refresh time is a nightmare. Build the process once, run it each April.
